name: Lymphadenopathy (oncology context)
description: Lymphadenopathy is enlargement of one or more lymph nodes beyond their normal size (generally >1 cm for most regions, >1.5 cm for inguinal nodes). In an oncology context, it represents either primary lymph node malignancy (lymphoma, leukaemia) or metastatic spread from a solid tumour. Worrying features include firmness or rubbery texture, non-tender nodes, nodes fixed to underlying structures, progressive enlargement over weeks, nodes in unusual locations (supraclavicular, epitrochlear), and constitutional B-symptoms. Supraclavicular lymphadenopathy in particular carries high malignancy risk and warrants urgent evaluation.
